card.description: Client-side hash-chain verification, D3.js supply-chain graphs and zero-trust auth for a sensitive Earth Observation data pipeline. Sole frontend engineer.

projects.title: DeepTrace.
projects.lede: A zero-trust data provenance platform for Earth Observation data. It verifies file lineage and integrity in the browser, without ever transferring the sensitive files.
challenge: Earth Observation data is sensitive and massive. Providers and consumers need to verify that nothing was tampered with between collection, processing and delivery, but the files themselves often can’t move across networks.

DeepTrace solves this by doing the verification client-side: the browser fetches a cryptographic hash chain, reconstructs the lineage graph, and validates each step against trusted sources, without the operator ever holding the raw data.

contributions.title: Lineage visualization in D3.js
contributions.body: Interactive force-directed graph of provenance. Each node is a processing step; edges are hash-verified transforms. Supports 1000+ nodes with zoom, pan, and query-based highlighting.

contributions.title: Client-side hash-chain verifier
contributions.body: Pure-browser cryptographic integrity check. Walks the chain from leaf to root, validates each SHA-256 hash against a trusted anchor, flags any tampered link with precise diagnostics.

contributions.title: Zero-trust auth with Cognito
contributions.body: AWS Cognito OAuth flow; access tokens never reach the server. Scoped permissions for data providers vs. consumers, with session-level hash-chain verification gating sensitive operations.

contributions.title: Vue 3 + Vite + Shadcn stack
contributions.body: Set up the project from scratch. Strict TypeScript, automated linting, pnpm workspaces, CI with preview deploys. Established patterns the rest of the team adopted.

projects.title: Kreditožrouti.
projects.lede: A course scheduler for VŠE students, live at kreditozrouti.cz. I created it and run it alone, from the InSIS scraping to the deployments. The numbers are modest on purpose: it quietly saves a few students their semester, every day.
challenge: Kreditožrouti is a course scheduler for students at the Prague University of Economics and Business. It scrapes public InSIS course data and puts a faster, clearer layer of search and scheduling on top, so a student can close a gap in their timetable in seconds instead of clicking through the university system.

It was never a startup, and the metrics are modest on purpose: a few hundred students, a handful of them every day, found mostly through Discord, Facebook and word of mouth. Alongside my client work, it is the one product I own end to end: live, maintained and still gaining users.

contributions.title: InSIS scraping and scheduling
contributions.body: Scrapes public InSIS course data and puts better search and scheduling on top of it than the university system offers, so a student can fill a gap in their timetable in seconds. The name is a joke that means something: when a timetable is set badly, courses eat your ECTS credits. Credit-gobblers.

contributions.title: From hackathon to product
contributions.body: Born at the 4FIS Mini Hackathon on live scraped data, a working MVP in 3.5 hours, first place. When the course that later hosted it ended, I picked it up and carried it alone to a finished product rather than a demo.

contributions.title: Production infrastructure
contributions.body: Runs today with monitoring, alerting and automatic deployments. Vue on the front, Node with Redis and BullMQ workers behind it, containerized with Docker and Traefik.

contributions.title: Bachelor thesis
contributions.body: The InSIS work led directly to my bachelor thesis: an MCP server over InSIS data, hosted on university servers under an official domain.

nodes.name: Web app

nodes.name: MCP server
nodes.tech: MCP SDK · tools over course data

architecture.observability: Observability: Alloy → Prometheus and Loki → Grafana. Alertmanager → Discord. Umami for analytics.
architecture.caption: A pnpm and Turborepo monorepo. The API owns every database write. The scraper only fetches and parses InSIS, then hands results back over a queue, so a slow university server never blocks a student's search. The MCP server reads the same MySQL data for AI clients and my bachelor thesis.
architecture.textAlternative: The browser loads the Vue app and calls the API through Traefik. The API reads and writes MySQL and queues scrape jobs in Redis. A scraper worker takes jobs from Redis, fetches InSIS course pages and returns results through Redis. AI clients reach a separate MCP server through Traefik; it only reads MySQL.

projects.title: Scorecard.
projects.lede: A security audit reporting tool built for cyber professionals. It turns risk analysis data into fully branded PDF reports in minutes.
challenge: Scorecard is a web application built for CORAC Engineering that functions as an interactive spreadsheet for cyber auditors, built for risk analysis data entry and report generation. The challenge was creating a tool that could replace ad-hoc spreadsheets while adding professional output capabilities without requiring a backend database. The result is a portable, offline-capable application that exports audit results directly to white-labeled PDFs and supports NIS2 compliance workflows.

projects.title: Disenchantment.
projects.lede: A Minecraft plugin that reimagines the anvil, letting players remove and recover enchantments from items for deeper inventory strategy across versions 1.18 to 26.x.
challenge: Disenchantment is a Java-based Minecraft plugin built with the Spigot API that solves a longstanding vanilla limitation: once you apply an enchantment, it’s permanent. The plugin introduces a new mechanic allowing players to remove and recover enchantments from items via a redesigned anvil interaction, adding real strategic depth to item management. Built with a focus on compatibility and performance, it runs across Minecraft versions 1.18–26.x with zero dependencies and is open source on GitHub.

contributions.title: Enhanced Anvil Mechanics
contributions.body: Redesigned the vanilla anvil system to support enchantment removal and recovery, giving players fine-grained control over item management and enchantment strategy.

contributions.title: Multi-Version Compatibility
contributions.body: Ensured seamless compatibility across Minecraft 1.18 through 26.x with no additional dependencies, enabling wide adoption on both legacy and current servers.

contributions.title: Custom GUI & Command System
contributions.body: Implemented user-friendly inventory interfaces and in-game commands with permission-based controls and detailed player feedback for smooth interaction.

contributions.title: Performance & Thread Safety
contributions.body: Applied best practices for thread safety and performance including asynchronous processing for item validation and enchantment data handling within the Spigot event system.
